options: Cutting off trade, marriage and social contact
questions.explain: Quraysh imposed a boycott on Banu Hashim and Banu Abdul Muttalib.

questions.q: How long were the Muslims besieged in Shi'b Abi Talib?
questions.explain: They lived in tents in isolation for almost five years, enduring hunger and thirst.

questions.q: Who was Khadijah's nephew who sent a camel loaded with food at night?
questions.explain: Hakim bin Hizam smuggled in food and later embraced Islam.

questions.q: Who stirred up opposition to the boycott by persuading people one by one?
questions.explain: Hisham bin Amr persuaded people until a group opposing the boycott was formed.

questions.q: Where did Zuhayr and his companions stand up to reject the boycott agreement?
questions.explain: Dar an-Nadwah was the assembly hall of the Quraysh chiefs in front of the Kaaba.

questions.q: What did the termites not eat on the agreement?
options: The name of the Prophet SAW
questions.explain: Only the name of Allah remained. Allah sends help in small ways.

questions.q: Which of the Prophet's uncles was the only one who did not join the siege?
questions.explain: Abu Lahab supported Abu Jahal and was not besieged.

questions.q: The Prophet SAW mentioned the favours of Mut'im bin Adi even though he did not embrace Islam.
questions.explain: True. We appreciate those who help us even if they are not Muslim.

questions.q: Tiny termites can undo a great agreement by Allah's permission.
questions.explain: True. Allah sends help in small ways.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: The agreement is eaten by termites
The agreement is hung in the Kaaba

questions.explain: The boycott was decided, the agreement hung, opponents organised, termites ate it, and the boycott ended.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: The assembly hall of the Quraysh chiefs
Cutting off trade and social ties

questions.explain: A boycott cuts off ties, a shi'b is a valley, Dar an-Nadwah was the Quraysh assembly hall, and a tribe is a clan.

questions.q: What lesson about supporting injustice does this story give?
options: Injustice is fine if many do it
Worse is the Muslim who supports injustice
questions.explain: Do not support injustice or mock refugees.
